project.name: assimp
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO checkout inspected here is `91cb2947ace52bcd9d297171bd9b66f5203370b5`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. Its line map matches the saved UBSan crash at `OpenDDLParserUtils.h:321` and the stack frames at `OpenDDLParser.cpp:549/527/293/431/346/234`, so the anchors below are resolved against this staged vulnerable tree.

classification.classification_note: The reproduced undefined behavior is an out-of-bounds table read in `isNumeric()`: a signed `char` name byte `0x80` is sign-extended, converted to a huge `size_t`, and then used as an unchecked index into `const unsigned char chartype_table[256]`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42500529 (assimp): Index-out-of-bounds found by fuzz target assimp_fuzzer [ubsan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42500529
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged assimp worktree
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is a 72-byte file that the fuzzer passes to `Importer::ReadFileFromMemory()`. OpenGEX signature detection routes it into `OpenGEXImporter::InternReadFile()`, which copies the raw bytes into `OpenDDLParser::m_buffer` and starts parsing. After the leading `ur{` is accepted, the parser re-enters `parseNextNode()` on the nested token starting at byte 3. `parseIdentifier()` consumes bytes 3-21 as the nested node identifier and stops at attacker-controlled byte 22, `$`. `parseName()` treats that `$` as a name introducer, advances to byte 23, and calls `parseIdentifier()` for the name. On the reproduced build, byte 23 is exactly `0x80`, so `parseIdentifier()` immediately evaluates `isNumeric(*in)` to forbid a numeric-leading name. `isNumeric()` casts that signed `char` to `size_t` and, with no range check, reads `chartype_table[18446744073709551488]`, which is the saved UBSan `index out of bounds for type 'const unsigned char [256]'` at `OpenDDLParserUtils.h:321`. The staged fix closes this exact obligation by introducing `idx < sizeof(chartype_table)` before the table access.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled file into parser-owned state. This copy preserves the exact `$ 0x80` byte pair later reinterpreted as a name introducer followed by the first name byte.
source.value_from: `gt_results/arvo_42500529/poc` is the exact 72-byte witness. After `OpenGEXImporter::InternReadFile()` reads it into a local `buffer`, this copy stores the bytes unchanged into `m_buffer`, including `m_buffer[22] == '$'` and `m_buffer[23] == 0x80` on the crashing path.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: UBSan crash site. `isNumeric()` indexes the 256-byte `chartype_table` with the sign-extended first name byte and performs the out-of-bounds table read reported in the saved trace.
sink.note: Stage 01 reproduced `runtime error: index 18446744073709551488 out of bounds for type 'const unsigned char [256]'` at this exact line, and frame 0 of the saved stack is `bool ODDLParser::isNumeric<char const>(char const)`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `isNumeric()` uses `static_cast<size_t>(in)` directly as a table index with no unsigned-byte normalization or `idx < sizeof(chartype_table)` guard, even though callers pass signed `char` values from the input buffer.
root_cause.note: For the witness, `parseName()` advances to byte `0x80`, `parseIdentifier()` calls `isNumeric(*in)`, and the cast produces the saved huge index `18446744073709551488`. The fix hunk keeps the cast but introduces `size_t idx` plus `idx < sizeof(chartype_table)` before reading the table.

parser_admitted.description: OpenGEX signature detection has already selected the OpenGEX importer by this point. This call admits the witness into the OpenDDL parser, and every project frame in the saved UBSan stack from frame 0 through frame 9 stays on that parser/importer path.

tainted_value_origin.description: This increment moves the current token pointer from the attacker-controlled `$` delimiter to the following byte, which becomes the first character of the candidate name identifier passed to `parseIdentifier()` and then to `isNumeric()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In the exact witness, the nested header bytes at offsets 22-23 are `$ 0x80`, so after this increment the next dereference sees `*in == 0x80`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The parser copies the entire attacker-controlled file into `m_buffer`. On the witnessed path this preserves the later-critical bytes `m_buffer[22] == '$'` and `m_buffer[23] == 0x80` exactly.

After the outer `ur{` header is already open, the body token beginning at `m_buffer[3]` is not recognized as a primitive data type, so the parser takes the complex-data branch and recurses into `parseNextNode()` on the nested bytes beginning `indexarray...$...`.

The nested node-type scan starts at `m_buffer[3]` and treats `$` as a terminator. For this witness it consumes bytes 3-21 as the nested header identifier and returns with `in` positioned on byte 22, the attacker-controlled `$` delimiter.

Because byte 22 is `$`, `parseName()` takes the name branch instead of returning. The increment advances `in` to byte 23, so the subsequent `parseIdentifier()` call sees the raw attacker byte `0x80` as the first character of the name identifier.

Before accepting any name characters, `parseIdentifier()` performs the 'identifier must not start with a digit' check by calling `isNumeric()` on the first byte supplied by step 4. On the witnessed path that byte is exactly `0x80`.

The helper converts the first name byte from `const char` to `size_t`. UBSan's reported index proves that, on this reproduced build, the input byte `0x80` is treated as signed `-128` before conversion, yielding `idx == 18446744073709551488` instead of `128`.

Root cause and sink. The code immediately dereferences `chartype_table[idx]` with the huge index from step 6 and has no `idx < sizeof(chartype_table)` guard. That out-of-bounds table read is exactly the saved UBSan `index out of bounds for type 'const unsigned char [256]'` at line 321.

crash_stack.function: Assimp::Importer::ReadFileFromMemory(void const*, unsigned long, unsigned int, char const*)

format.name: raw 72-byte binary OpenDDL/OpenGEX-like file
format.contract: The witness is the exact 72-byte file in `gt_results/arvo_42500529/poc`. The verified trigger facts are: bytes 0-2 are `75 72 7b` (`ur{`), bytes 3-21 are consumed as the next nested header token, byte 22 is exactly `$`, byte 23 is exactly `0x80`, and the parser later reaches `parseName()` on that `$`. That exact `$ 0x80` pair makes `parseName()` treat `$` as a name introducer and then makes `parseIdentifier()` call `isNumeric()` on `0x80` as the first name byte, yielding the saved table index `18446744073709551488`. This contract does not generalize beyond that exact 72-byte witness and its observed `$ 0x80` name-prefix condition.
